name: infra_serving
title: Serving only: a TorchServe handler and a FastAPI app, with no training anywhere
origin: hardening round 1, tester domain-infra: the must-not-claim-a-training-loop negative
note: This package has no optimizer, no loss, no backward() and no .fit(); the only loops are over an incoming request batch. MLView reports nothing and declares data, objective and train ABSENT, which is correct and is the claim this program exists to check. It does report `eval` present, because it maps a prediction call into the Evaluate lane - a modelling choice, not a claim that the project measures anything.
stagesObserved: config, preprocess, model, eval, deliver present; data, objective and train reported absent.

forbidden.why: there is no optimizer and no backward() in this package; nothing trains
same: there is no .backward() whose gradients could go unapplied
nothing accumulates a loss; postprocess collects floats out of topk
initialize() calls self.model.eval() at line 60 and inference() carries @torch.no_grad() at line 73
the lifespan hook calls model.eval() at line 34 and predict() runs inside `with torch.no_grad():` at line 68
the forward pass is inside `with torch.no_grad():` at line 68
torch.softmax at line 76 is applied to produce probabilities for the response; there is no CrossEntropyLoss anywhere in this package to double-log-softmax them
same: the softmax at line 70 feeds the HTTP response, not a loss
preprocess() moves the stacked batch with .to(self.device) at line 71 and initialize() moves the model at line 59
the batch is moved with .to(_state["device"]) at line 67 and the model at line 33
there is no training, no split and no random source in this package, so there is nothing for a seed to pin down - MLV601's own gate requires training evidence
ProductTagger.__init__ calls super().__init__() as its first statement
torch.load at line 56 passes both map_location= and weights_only=True
torch.load at line 31 passes both map_location= and weights_only=True
